name: CDMem (Context-Dependent Memory Framework for LLM-Centric Agents)
venue: NAACL 2025 (Volume 3: Industry Track), Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the ACL: Human Language Technologies; pages 1055-1069; DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.naacl-industry.80
authors_affiliation: Pengyu Gao (Independent Researcher), Jinming Zhao (Qiyuan Lab, corresponding author), Xinyue Chen (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics), Yilin Long (Peking University). Pengyu Gao and Jinming Zhao contributed equally.
task_domain: Interactive decision-making / embodied text-game agents (navigation and manipulation in situated virtual textual environments).
problem_setting: Online, interactive single-agent decision-making over multi-trial episodes. An LLM-centric agent (GPT-4o-mini or GPT-4o) interacts with situated text environments, generating reasoning-and-action trajectories. The system is an online learning architecture that continuously learns and updates memory during deployment (no separate offline training phase, unlike Expel/AutoGuide). 5 trials per environment, max 20 interaction steps per trial. Supervision is from environment success/failure feedback (verbal/textual), not labeled gold demonstrations.
what_is_retrieved: Multilevel knowledge: expert-encoded raw trajectories (CD-exemplars), short-term task experiences (successful shortcuts, failure-type reflections, environmental summaries), and long-term insights (environmental insights, success- and failure-related task insights).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes during deployment (online learning). The retrievable store is induced and continuously updated at test time from the agent's own trajectories; not a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed-count retrieval driven by similarity/match: retrieves a fixed number of exemplars (all methods use two exemplars) and a fixed number L of insights re-ranked by cosine similarity. It is context-match-gated (intersection of env-match and task-match prioritized) rather than a complete-minimal-set or precision-driven variable-size objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] — Retrieve (context-dependent graph index matching), Reuse (retrieved exemplars/insights injected into prompt for action decisions), Revise (short-term reflection on success/failure refines experiences; long-term encoding consolidates), Retain (online write-back into Env-Index/Task-Index). Not framed as CBR by the authors.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work is framed via human cognitive memory psychology (context-dependent effect, encoding/storage/retrieval) and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it realizes CBR-like retrieve-reuse-revise-retain mechanisms under a memory-framework framing.
retrieval_unit: Multiple units organized by a graph index: (i) raw interaction trajectories / expert-compressed trajectories used as exemplars (CD-exemplars); (ii) task experiences (successful shortcuts, failure-type reflections); (iii) distilled guideline-style insights (environmental insights and success/failure task insights). Effectively trajectory + experience + guideline-rule granularities keyed by environment-type and task-type.
index_source: Online/test-time-induced growing memory. Memory is encoded from the agent's own trials during deployment via multistage encoding (expert -> short-term -> long-term every B tasks) and stored into the context-dependent index; the store grows and updates online.
index_structure_topology: Graph-structured, context-dependent index composed of two dictionaries: Env-Index (environment-dependent long-term memories) and Task-Index (task-dependent, split into Success and Failure sub-dictionaries). Keys are environment/task descriptions (types predefined by domain experts); values are short-term-memory + raw-trajectory pairs. Retrieval matches on environment-type and task-type cues (metadata/context-keyed graph).
retriever_type: Hybrid: LLM-as-retriever for index matching (prompt-based Index Matching Module M_match selects best environment/task type) plus dense embedding cosine-similarity (text-embedding-3-small) for non-LLM re-ranking of insights.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The index-matching is a zero-shot prompted LLM module; the re-ranking uses fixed cosine similarity over off-the-shelf embeddings (text-embedding-3-small). No trained/contrastive/RL retriever.
query_construction: The current trial's environment description and task goal are used as the query/cue. The prompt-based Index Matching Module takes the current task and environment as input and outputs the best-matching environment-type and task-type, which serve as keys to access the graph index.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at the start of a new trial): retrieval is performed per new trial conditioned on its environment description and task goal, not per reasoning step.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot per trial: at the inference/start of a new trial the agent retrieves relevant exemplars and insights once and injects them into the working-memory prompt for the episode.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (deterministic): retrieval is triggered at the start of each new trial via the index-matching module on the current task/environment cues; there is no token-confidence, uncertainty, or learned-router trigger.
reranking: Yes. A non-LLM-based sorting/re-ranking algorithm (Rerank, Algorithm 3) computes cosine similarity between each candidate insight and the short-term memories of the current environment/task and sums the scores to prioritize the most relevant insights. Exemplars are prioritized by env-task intersection match.
retrieved_context_refinement: rerank (cosine-similarity-based insight sorting) plus context-match filtering (prioritize exemplars in the env/task intersection, fall back to Task-Index then default Reflexion exemplars). The encoding stages also distill/compress trajectories before storage (expert encoding compresses raw trajectories).
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/API retrieval; not a tool-use setting).
index_content_separation: Yes (partial): the graph index keys are lightweight environment/task descriptions while the heavy content (raw trajectories and short-term memories) is stored as the dictionary values and recalled on demand after match; expert encoding compresses raw trajectories into a lighter knowledge chunk before storage.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol; memory index is updated in-process online).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; not a tool-use setting).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / case reuse: retrieved CD-exemplars, environmental insights, and success/failure task insights are organized together with the current trial and task experiences into a working-memory-style prompt and fed to the LLM to make action decisions.
planning_integration: One-shot retrieve-then-act at the start of each trial: relevant exemplars and insights are retrieved and assembled into the prompt (working memory) which then drives interleaved ReAct-style reasoning-and-action decisions across the episode. Not inside MCTS/tree search; not per-step retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-trial (per-episode): retrieval happens once per trial and the retrieved context conditions the whole reasoning-acting rollout; reasoning and acting themselves are interleaved (ReAct) but without per-step re-retrieval.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation plus execution-feedback-driven revision: retrieved insights/exemplars guide the LLM's action decisions (verbatim-style ICL exemplars), and short-term encoding revises experiences by reflecting on successful (build 'Successful Shortcut') and unsuccessful (classify error type: planning/search/operation) trajectories; long-term encoding consolidates these into cross-task insights.
retrieved_item_representation: Mixed surface forms injected as text: raw/expert-compressed trajectories (exemplars), distilled free-text insights/guidelines (environmental insights, success/failure task insights), and structured task experiences (successful shortcuts, failure-type reflections, environmental summaries).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Multilevel: raw trajectory (exemplars), expert-compressed trajectory, short-term task experiences/shortcuts, and distilled cross-task insights/guidelines (environmental and task insights) — spanning concrete demonstrations up to abstract state-aware guideline-like insights.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Context-dependent indexing restricts retrieval to environment/task-type-matched memory (key-cue gating) to avoid irrelevant recall; insight re-ranking by cosine similarity to current short-term memories filters and prioritizes relevant insights; authors report insights significantly reduce agent hallucinations (e.g., correct item-usage context in ALFWorld). No explicit retriever-aware adversarial training.
memory_type: graph (context-dependent graph-structured index) combining episodic trajectories, short-term experience, and long-term distilled insights/guidelines.
write_back: True. New encoded memories (short-term experiences and, after batching, long-term insights) are written back into the Env-Index and Task-Index dictionaries; trajectories are retained as exemplars.
online_growth: True. CDMem is explicitly an online learning framework; the retrievable store grows and updates during deployment as the agent encounters novel environments/tasks (contrasted with offline Expel/AutoGuide).
write_back_trigger: On-success-and-failure plus batched reflective consolidation: short-term encoding writes after each trial reflecting separately on successful and unsuccessful trajectories; long-term Memory Encoding Module fires every B tasks (batch size, e.g. default 1; experiments up to 11) to consolidate accumulated short-term memories into long-term insights and update the indices.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure are stored and used separately. The Task-Index has explicit Success and Failure sub-dictionaries; short-term encoding produces 'Successful Shortcuts' from successes and error-type (planning/search/operation) reflections from failures; long-term task insights summarize positive and negative examples separately (common mistakes and remedies from failures).
memory_evolution_update: append-and-consolidate: short-term memories appended to per-key lists; when a list reaches batch size, long-term encoding processes (consolidates/abstracts) entries into long-term insights stored in the indices, and long-term encoding 'updates memory indexes to maintain relevance and accuracy' (delta-update / re-consolidation rather than pure append-only).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is a fixed prompted index-matching + fixed cosine-similarity re-ranking; it is not an RL/learned retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing described.
benchmarks: ALFWorld (134 test environments, composed of 9 rooms and 6 task types, following the ReAct/Reflexion/Expel split) and ScienceWorld (50-task test set: 10 task types whose oracle trajectory average length < 20 steps, top 5 variants each).
benchmark_family: embodied / interactive decision-making text environments (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld).
baselines: ReAct (no-memory baseline), Reflexion, Expel-Online, AutoGuide-Online. (Expel and AutoGuide are originally offline; the paper compares against their online variants.)
key_metrics: Task success rate (%) on ALFWorld; average score on ScienceWorld. Also reports computational cost (API calls per sample, total API calls, monetary cost) and success-rate-vs-number-of-trials curves.
headline_result: Using GPT-4o-mini, CDMem reaches 85.8% success rate on ALFWorld and 56.0 (56.02) score on ScienceWorld, surpassing state-of-the-art online LLM-centric methods. With Configuration 2 (memory components on GPT-4o), ALFWorld success rate reaches 90.0%, nearly 10 points above Expel-Online's 80.3%; on ScienceWorld CDMem's 56.02 exceeds AutoGuide-Online's 44.84 by over 10 points.
ablations: ALFWorld ablations (Table 1): full CDMem 85.8; w/o expert encoding 72.3 (~10pt drop, largest impact alongside env insights); w/o task-encoding 84.3; w/o env-encoding 74.3 (~10pt drop); w/o CD-Exemplars 80.6 (~5pt drop). ScienceWorld ablations (Table 2): full 56.0; w/o task-encoding 40.9; w/o env-encoding 54.7 (only ~2pt drop). Batch-size study (Table 6): SR stable across batch sizes 1-11 (83.6-86.4), demonstrating CDMem tolerates larger insight-extraction batches than Expel/AutoGuide. Analyses: expert encoding before short-term encoding yields more accurate successful-shortcut summaries; env/task insights reduce hallucinations.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (success rate / score) plus cost are reported; no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) for the index-matching or re-ranking are reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (success rate / score). Some process-oriented analysis is provided: success-rate-vs-trial-number curves (improvement between trial 0 and trial 1) and qualitative hallucination-reduction analysis, but no quantitative step-wise retrieval/planning accuracy.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported (Table 3, ALFWorld vs Reflexion): CDMem uses 4 API calls per sample vs Reflexion's 2; 1155 total API calls vs 781; monetary cost $0.51 vs $0.33 for processing the dataset. Authors frame CDMem as efficient given its accuracy gains; batch-size analysis shows insight extraction remains effective at larger batches, reducing long-term-encoding cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k injection: all methods use two exemplars; a fixed number L of insights is retrieved then re-ranked by cosine similarity (reranked-then-selected). Max 20 interaction steps per trial. Exemplar selection prioritizes env-task intersection, falling back to Task-Index then default Reflexion exemplars.
benchmark_construction_and_size: ALFWorld test set reuses the established 134-environment split (9 rooms x 6 task types) from ReAct/Reflexion/Expel. ScienceWorld test set is newly constructed: from 30 ScienceWorld task types, select 10 types with oracle average trajectory length < 20, take top 5 variants each -> 50 environments; answer verifiability via environment-defined success/score. Best-system scores (CDMem 85.8% ALFWorld GPT-4o-mini; 56.0 ScienceWorld) signal task difficulty.
builds_on: Reflexion (verbal RL reflection; CDMem's short-term encoding extends it and uses its default exemplars as fallback), ReAct (interleaved reasoning+acting backbone and ALFWorld test split), Expel and AutoGuide (offline experience/insight and state-aware guideline extraction, extended to online here).
contrasts_with: Expel-Online and AutoGuide-Online (offline experience/guideline learners; CDMem is online and continuously self-improving), Reflexion (reflects only on failures and uses fixed exemplars; CDMem reflects on successes and failures with context-dependent exemplars), and memory methods like MemoryBank/ChatDB/TiM that retrieve directly from the whole memory pool without an efficient context-dependent index.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience-based planning): online experience/memory-based LLM agents that retrieve self-generated trajectories, experiences, and distilled insights to improve interactive decision-making; sits in the Reflexion -> Expel/AutoGuide lineage, adding human-memory-inspired multistage encoding and a context-dependent graph index for online learning.
